Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
Today Anthropic, PBC launched the roadshow for its proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock.
The proposed offering consists of 825,000,000 shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 801,351,354 shares are being offered by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders. Anthropic also expects to grant the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares of its Class A common stock.
The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”
The proposed offering will be made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained from: Goldman Sachs & Co. items.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
items.detailText:
Today, we’re excited to introduce Muse Spark 1.1, the latest model from Meta Superintelligence Labs and a significant upgrade from Muse Spark. Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.
With these improvements, Muse Spark 1.1 advances the performance-efficiency frontier. Together with this week’s launch of Muse Image , this release brings us closer to our vision of personal superintelligence: models that help you pursue your goals, create what you imagine, deepen your relationships, and take action on what you value most.
Along with this release, we are launching a public preview of the new Meta Model API where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1. The model is available now in "Thinking" mode in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai .
For more details about our evaluations, see our report .
Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services. It zero-shot generalizes to new native tools, MCP servers, and custom skills.
It tackles complex projects significantly faster than Muse Spark, as it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency. As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents. As a subagent, it adheres to its job, understands available tools, and knows when to escalate back to the main agent.
Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens. It remembers actions, retrieves information from much earlier work, and compacts in a way that keeps the critical steps needed for later work.
Muse Spark 1.1 excels at computer-use workflows that unfold across multiple applications with information changing on-the-fly. It maintains context across extended sessions, adapts to evolving requirements, and navigates unfamiliar interfaces with minimal human intervention.
Rather than reasoning through every desktop step one click at a time, Muse Spark 1.1 understands when to automate and when to use the interface directly. We trained the model to write scripts when automation is faster, click when direct interaction is simpler, and generate batches of actions at each step.

items.title: Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video
items.detailText:
Muse Image follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, composes from multiple references, and draws on Instagram for social context. Muse...
We’re excited to launch Muse Image and preview Muse Video, the first media generation models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Image is our most advanced image generation model yet: it follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, and composes from multiple references. It also brings agentic tool use capabilities and integrates with Muse Spark. Muse Video, built on the same pretraining base, delivers exceptional visual fidelity with native audio support.
Muse Image is available today across the Meta AI app and on meta.ai , Instagram Stories in the US, and WhatsApp in limited countries, and is coming soon to Facebook. Muse Video is coming soon to creators and Meta AI.
Instead of directly mapping prompts to images, Muse Image operates as an agent: it invokes search and coding tools to improve accuracy, self-refines its own generations, and improves through scaling test-time compute. Muse Image also integrates with Muse Spark, allowing the two models to share tools and plan jointly for powerful agentic media generation.
We provide Muse Image with access to tools to enhance its agentic capabilities.
Coding. During reinforcement learning, Muse Image learns to write and execute code that produces accurate plots and QR codes, and condition on rendered figures to improve the accuracy of generated images. Muse Spark and Muse Image also integrate to use the combination of code and media generation to create animated GIFs, websites with embedded images, and interactive visual games.
Search. Muse Image learns to search the web to ground generated images in factual and real-time information and visual references. Enabling search improves factual accuracy on knowledge-intensive prompts, particularly those involving current events and real-world facts.
Muse Image improves with search tool use. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image reflects on and improves upon its own work within its chain of thought. This self-refining behavior can take different forms: a local edit to the current image draft when a small detail is off, a new image generation from scratch when larger parts are wrong, or a different tactic like tool use for more factually accurate generation. We didn’t design this behavior. Instead, it emerged during RL training simply because self-refinement produced better images and therefore higher reward.
Muse Image improves with emergent self-refinement. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image improves with scaling test-time compute. Elo from internal ablation.
Muse Image edits images with precision, changing exactly what the user asks for. It can follow a variety of instruction

items.title: 一次性收入撑起超预期，算力延期才是真问题
items.detailText:
一次性收入撑起超预期，算力延期才是真问题
AI 新云 Nebius(NBIS.US) 于美东时间 11 月 12 日盘前 发榜 了三季度财报。乍看本季业绩相当不错，增长和盈利都明显好于预期，GAAP 经营利润也首次转正。
但 CoreWeave 的强劲财报后，NBIS 次日已跟涨约 15%，提前计价了本季业绩会好；而细看本季实际有多处不小的问题：
最最最关键的地方： 算力上线延期导致 4Q 收入指引显著低于预期，RPO 环比几乎没有增长，对 27 年的指引也不算惊喜。
3Q26 收入 9.8 亿美元，单季净增约 4 亿美元，稍高于一致预期的 9.3 亿。其中 AI 云收入 9.7 亿，占集团约 99%。
不过其中约 3.3 亿是轻资产模式下首期合作的一次性启用收入，公司预计这类收入以后会更常态化。
且实际上本季算力建设进度有所延误， 营收看似超预期、可能更多是此一次性收入的影响，含金量不高。
季末 ARR 约 64 亿美元，较 6 月末的 30 亿翻倍，比一致预期高近四成；但推测也含这笔一次性收入的 “误导”。
公司本季宣布此后不再用 ARR 衡量业务， 原先预计年末达到的 70~90 亿的 ARR 目标，也推迟为明年 2 月超过 70 亿。
3Q 新签合同的每 MW 年化收入超 2,500 万美元，vs 上季的超 2,000 万，每 GPU 小时价格比 2Q 平均高 20% 以上。同时，公司再度强调 3~6 个月的短期集群价格是签约合同价的两倍以上。
同时， 本季订单量的增长明显放缓： 季末 RPO 约 387 亿美元，环比仅 +3%（约 12 亿）。这表明要么公司把算力更多留给了灵活定价的短约，要么是公司在 3Q 时签单遇到了问题。
所幸，公司称 3Q 至今新签合同额超 120 亿美元 （含数十亿美元的 5 年期合同） ， 其中多数在季末之后才签订 、会体现在 4Q 的 RPO 里， 签单有所回暖。
本季 多个第三方托管站点的交付推迟到 2027 年上半年 。其中新泽西为微软建设的项目，年底前交付合同产能的一半以上，剩余批次排到 2Q27。公司称 自建站点进度正常或提前 ，美国选举也不影响其自建和托管站点。
公司下调 4Q 营收指引和 ARR 到达 70 亿的时间点， 背后应当就是算力建设的延期。这 对要和时间赛跑、高效完成从融资到投产创收的新云公司是一个重大问题。
Capex 方面，本季约 73 亿美元，环比增近 30% 但与一致预期基本持平，约为收入的 7 倍。按占收入的倍数，看似 Capex 投入力度走低，但若剔除轻资产模式的一次性收入，实际达云租赁收入的约 11 倍。
由于高额的 Capex，且本季经营现金流为−2.7 亿美元 ( vs. 前两个季度均净流入约 22.5 亿)，导致 本季自由现金流出约 76 亿，大幅不及预期。
由于现金走低，且本季新增负债约 57 亿，使得公司的 资产负债结构，从净现金转为净负债约 55 亿美元 。虽然公司此前以股权融资为主，但在巨额的支出压力下 ，资产负债结构还是出现了拐点性的恶化。
本季经营现金流偏低主要是应收账款明显增加约 38 亿，即客户的实际现金付款有所迟滞。
所幸和 CoreWeave 的情况类似，公司表示 3Q 签订的一年以上合同额中超 90% 带预付款 ， 预付款已能覆盖对应合同所需 Capex 的 100% （上季 50%~60%）。在相当程度上 能减轻之后的现金流压力。
同时，公司宣布首次签下 AI 云的 5 年期合同（均为老客户在新产能上的扩容），并新增 Databricks、Datadog、Snowflake 等非 AI Lab 客户的多年合同。客户结构继续多元化。
集团调整后 EBITDA 4.7 亿美元，利润率 47.5%，比一致预期的利润率高约 9pct，连续三个季度提升；其中 AI 云分部调整后 EBITDA 利润率 53.2% vs. 上季 49.7%。 同时 GAAP 经营利润 达 0.5 亿，也首次转正。
但超预期背后有两个 “水分”。一是约 3.3 亿的轻资产一次性收入 ：公司 2Q 介绍这一模式时就称 其利润率高 、几乎不需要资本投入。 二是折旧 ：本季为 3.5 亿美元，比一致预期低约四成，占收入比从上季的 44.6% 降到 36.2%。
推测主要是 算力建设延期、导致大量资产尚未投用、未开始计提折旧 ，GAAP 经营利润的超预期大部分来自这里；因此等推迟的产能上线，折旧会明显跳升。
CFO 称 4Q 要先承担新站点上线前的租金、电力和人员成本， 全年约 40% 的利润率指引隐含 4Q 回落到 35% 左右。
由于部分第三方产能推迟到 2027 年上半年（公司称对应合同仍在），26 全年收入指引从 30~34 亿美元下调到 30~32 亿美元 ，隐含 4Q 收入约 10.4~12.4 亿，比一致预期低约 17%~31% 。
按指引的全年 EBITDA 利润率，隐含 4Q 利润率约 35%~36%，同样不及预期。
而全年 capex 则上调到约 270 亿美元， 隐含 4Q Capex 约 116 亿，比一致预期高约 27%，收入增长放缓，投入则要继续加速 ；年末签约电力 5GW 的目标不变。
收入 120~130 亿美元（约为今年的 4 倍），中值 比一致预期低约 1% ，公司称对建设节奏的假设偏保守；
Capex 400~450 亿美元，中值比一致预期高约 34%， 同样是收入增长没惊喜，但投入却越来越高；
所幸，预期 27 年客户预付款 170~200 亿美元，连同以长合同做抵押的融资， 可覆盖 capex 的 75%~85%，后续投资基本都由客户承担。
预计 4Q27 实现税前盈亏平衡（含利息、未说明是否为 GAAP 口径）， 利润率转正节奏好于预期 。
本季乍看报表亮眼，实际问题却不少。收款和合同抵押贷款来覆盖 Capex 的利好，市场早已从 CoreWeave 的财报中得知并消化完毕，股价又已提前跟涨，本季财报属于已知利好落地 + 未知利空惊吓的组合。
上季大量新增 PPE 投入，本季并没转化为收入。直接原因是新泽西等第三方托管站点的电力问题—— 业主提前撤掉临时发电，替代的燃料电池爬坡跟不上。
10 月底以来，微软称部分第三方产能交付延迟，又传出新泽西项目推迟、微软收缩新云合作名单；而管理层称只是几个月的延迟，微软参与了排期调整， 合同仍在。
但从 2027 年起新增产能转向自建，建设风险将全部由公司自己承担， 上线节奏会是之后每个季度最重要的观察点。
3Q 入账的新订单不多，多笔大单在季末后才签；4Q 的收入和利润率又会受上线延期拖累。
明年的收入指引实现问题不大 ：管理层对上线时点的假设很保

供给端变量把国产算力推到台前
11月12日，英伟达董事会宣布，公司创始人黄仁勋已辞去总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务，即刻生效。现任执行副总裁兼首席财务官科莱特・克雷斯（Colette Kress）出任临时CEO，在正式继任者确定前继续兼任CFO；董事会同步启动新任CEO遴选，将同时考虑内部与外部候选人。董事会另任命哈维・C・琼斯（Harvey C.Jones）为首任董事会主席。
克雷斯自2013年9月加入英伟达以来，此前在思科、微软等科技公司从事财务工作近25年；琼斯有30余年企业家、科技高管与风险投资经历，曾任Synopsys首席执行官及执行董事长。黄仁勋1993年创办英伟达，执掌33年。
黄仁勋辞职消息引发资本市场震荡。11月12日美股盘前，英伟达股价一度跌逾10%，较前一交易日173.73美元的收盘价大幅回落，开盘后略有回升，截至美东时间10:15，英伟达股价为161.77美元，跌幅为6.88%。市场正在重新评估这家AI芯片巨头在失去创始人后的经营与治理风险。
全球AI产业更关心的是另一件事：黄仁勋离开后，英伟达的产品路线、客户关系和供应链承诺能否保持稳定？
“新上台的CEO第一件事或许是合规审查，查供应链与客户。”一位资深人士向《IT时报》记者表示，“过渡期管理层还要稳住的是客户与供应链预期，现有订单能不能按时交付、明年产能怎么排，比讲新故事更重要”。
官方公告称黄仁勋的贡献“意义深远”，董事会和公司“衷心感谢”，但截至发稿，黄仁勋本人并未公开发声，其卸任之后，对英伟达下游客户而言，需要重新盘算的已不是“英伟达还行不行”，而是“下一次扩容，卡从哪里来、多久能到位”。
11月4 日，谷歌宣布在马来西亚投资150亿美元扩建数据中心与云业务，新建园区落在雪兰莪与森美兰州，投资期为2027至2028年，约为其2024年20亿美元承诺的7.5倍；微软在吉隆坡附近的数据中心正在建设，其马来西亚投资规模为22亿美元，并于2025年5月开出印尼首个云区域；亚马逊云科技2025年初上线亚太（泰国）区域。
一部分中国企业还会依托自身资源与人脉，通过海外渠道采购服务器与加速卡。据财新报道，泰国已批复的约1.5GW数据中心项目中，带有中资背景或主要服务中资大厂客户的项目占比达60%至70%。
《IT时报》记者以买家身份向多个算力租赁渠道询价时，有渠道方表示，当前能够稳定对外出租的高端算力“越来越难锁定”，部分渠道对明年能否续约“不敢打包票”。
有服务器厂商人士告诉记者，东南亚、欧洲等地仍是现阶段部分客户获取海外算力的选择，但供给端的不确定性正在增加。除价格上涨外，客户还必须考虑合同续签、资源持续供应及未来监管政策变化等风险。
另一方面，英伟达高端算力在租赁市场依然抢手。部分复杂训练和高性能计算场景仍然优先选择英伟达GPU，短期内很难全面替代。但价格已成最直接的变量，渠道方发现，今年以来，咨询中国算力方案的客户明显增多。
2026年1月12日，美国众议院以369票赞成、22票反对通过《远程访问安全法案》。该法案试图弥补现行出口管制对远程访问先进计算资源的监管空白，核心是把出口管制的管辖对象从 “物项出境” 延伸到 “远程访问”。
截至11月，该法案尚未进入下一步立法程序，也未生效，但对于通过海外数据中心获取高端算力的企业而言，监管边界是否进一步向云端延伸，已经成为新的风险变量。
IDC 2026年上半年数据显示，中国数据中心AI加速器总出货约200.8万颗，其中GPU 99.1万颗、同比下降26%，含推理芯片在内的非GPU加速器101.6万颗、同比增长近80%，首次在出货量上超过GPU。英伟达出货67.8万颗、份额33.8%，同比下降44%；华为57.2万颗、份额28.5%；阿里平头哥13.3万颗、约7%；寒武纪9.2万颗、约5%；昆仑芯约4%；海光约3%；摩尔线程5.6万颗、约3%，在国产GPU厂商中居首。
多位业内人士向《IT时报》记者表示，目前国产卡梯队分层比较明确。第一梯队是华为昇腾与平头哥：前者规模领先，已进入政企、运营商与云体系的稳定部署；后者的产能首先服务阿里自身云与AI体系，外部客户增量有限。有业内人士向记者透露，平头哥去年有一部分旧型号流入市场，今年市面上已基本买不到它的卡，“拿货很难”；但从实际使用反馈看，其产品素质在业内口碑不低。
11月10日阿里巴巴公告称，已就分拆平头哥赴港交所主板独立上市提交分拆方案，平头哥已于9月11日以保密形式递交A1表格。如果分拆上市最终落地，平头哥有望获得更独立的融资渠道和更高的资本市场估值。但平头哥的真武芯片能否从主要服务阿里内部转向更大的外部供应，仍取决于产能、客户结构和商业策略。
沐曦、天数智芯、摩尔线程、燧原和壁仞科技同处第二梯队，其中沐曦与天数智芯位居该梯队头部，综合规模、生态成熟度与系统级交付能力相对靠前。
沐曦曦云C600配备144GB HBM3e显存，2026年5月量产，从设计、制造、封装到软件栈实现国产供应链闭环，并于上半年首批通过国家《安全可靠测评》。天数智芯天垓300在今年7月完成的第三方实测中，典型PD分离部署下折算单卡端到端吞吐达到国际主流高端GPU的1.05倍，据其披露为国内首个在该维度达到这一水平的通用GPU。
昆仑芯按出货量计份额约4%，仍处第二梯队，并在今年1月以保密形式向港交所递交上市申请，5月启动科创板上市辅导，A+H双通道推进；百度方面对 “昆仑芯上市时间推迟”的市场传闻回应称不属实。
摩尔线程8月9日发布的半年报显示，上半年营业收入17.36亿元、同比增长147.42%，已超2025年全年营收；归母净利润亏损1156.31万元，同比减亏。其出货量在国产GPU厂商中居首，生态成熟度与系统级交付经验仍在积累。
不过，英伟达经营面并未转弱。其2027财年第二季度（截至2026年7月26日）营收962.2亿美元、同比增长106%，数据中心业务收入为890亿美元、同比增长117%。官方公告称，第三季度财报仍将按原计划于11月17日发布。
供给的可预期性正在下降。企业当下要回答的问题，不再是“有没有卡”，而是“卡在谁手里、下次扩容能否到位”。面向国产算力的窗口能开多大，取决于第一梯队是否释放产能、第二梯队是否能把实测数字变成持续交付。
本文来自微信公众号 “IT时报”（ID：vittimes） ，作者：毛宇，编辑：郝俊慧 孙妍，36氪经授权发布。

items.detailText:
This article introduces Alibaba Cloud's full-stack AgenticOps platform, enabling autonomous, closed-loop AI operations and R&D through unified observability, evaluation, and controlled execution.
The upgraded Cloud Monitor 2.0, now with agentic observability, makes both the system and Agents legible. A complete Agent task breaks into three consecutive phases: trusted facts, evidence-based judgment, and controlled action. For observability by Agents, Cloud Monitor 2.0 hands production facts to the Agent through a single pipeline.
For governance, the observability pipeline runs through three stages — standardization, organization, and trustworthiness — turning raw observability data such as metrics, logs, traces, events, and metadata into production facts that carry their source, freshness, semantics, quality, and cost boundaries.
Once Agents can evolve themselves, the moat in enterprise AI shifts from whose model is better to whose evolution flywheel spins faster.
That chain rests on a unified operational context. Unified Connectors reach across Alibaba Cloud accounts, enterprise IDCs, and external systems; unified data modeling then brings metrics, logs, traces, events, changes, and code together with applications, instances, containers, and databases into one context that an Agent can understand and investigate.
Cloud Monitor 2.0, AgentLoop, STAROps, and Alibaba Cloud DevOps are product capabilities for enterprise production. Beyond them, Alibaba Cloud contributes to three open-source projects — OpenTelemetry (OTel), UModel, and BRiSE — to break, at the foundation, the three walls of data that cannot be collected, context that cannot be understood, and capabilities that cannot be verified, so the whole stack becomes a public asset the industry can reuse, verify, and build together.
When a system can perceive, decide, and turn every resolution into experience for the next one, the competitive question in enterprise AI becomes simple: who evolves faster.

items.title: Alibaba Cloud's Open-Source AI Agent Handbook, 3K+ GitHub Stars
items.description: Alibaba Cloud's Open-Source AI Agent Handbook, 3K+ GitHub Stars This article introduces Alibaba Cloud's open-source AI Agent Handbook, a practical guide for reliably deploying, governing, and integrating AI agents into real-world
items.detailText:
This article introduces Alibaba Cloud's open-source AI Agent Handbook, a practical guide for reliably deploying, governing, and integrating AI agents into real-world enterprise workflows.
As AI becomes easier to access, the enterprise challenge is no longer simply how to build an agent. It is how to make agents complete tasks reliably, fit into business workflows, and deliver outcomes people can trust. Alibaba Cloud's open-source AI Agent Handbook explores the engineering and organizational work needed to close that gap.
The AI Agent Handbook has surpassed 3,000 stars on GitHub. Its focus is a practical question: as intelligent capabilities become more widely available, how can organizations turn them into reliable results?
Advances in models are making understanding, reasoning, planning, and generation available through model calls. Capabilities that once depended entirely on human time and expertise are becoming more accessible. But greater access to AI does not automatically translate into greater productivity.
An agent may generate a plan, call a tool, and carry out an operation. That does not mean a business can safely hand it an important task. In a real workflow, the system must also track progress, know which actions have already taken effect, decide when to continue or stop, and identify who should approve the final result.
Moving from answering questions to delivering outcomes requires more than a better model. It changes how applications are organized and where engineering responsibilities lie.
Initiated by Alibaba Cloud, the handbook brings together architecture, agent construction, runtime infrastructure, governance, optimization, and enterprise case studies. It shifts the discussion from building agents quickly to making them useful and dependable in production.
As models and agents evolve, enterprise attention is shifting toward three connected challenges.
The first is production engineering . Model-generated judgments are probabilistic, while business deliverables need explicit acceptance criteria. A compelling response is not enough. A system must keep work moving when information is incomplete, tools fail, or task requirements change. It must also provide verifiable evidence that the final result meets the requirements.
The second is scale . As adoption expands from a few experiments to many users, teams, and concurrent tasks, trade-offs between reliability, security, performance, and cost become harder to ignore. A few extra rounds of inference may be acceptable in a trial. Repeated across a large workload, the same overhead can change the economics of the service.

items.title: Integrating Wan3.0 via API: Queues, Retries, and Cost Controls
items.description: Integrating Wan3.0 via API: Queues, Retries, and Cost Controls Every platform team wiring Wan3.0 into internal tools faces the same question: how do you integrate an asynchronous video generation API without payin... Johnny Mai
items.detailText:
Every platform team wiring Wan3.0 into internal tools faces the same question: how do you integrate an asynchronous video generation API without payin...
A client that re-sends the create call on every timeout does not fail loudly. In the worked example below it adds $900 to a $4,000 month of Wan3.0 video, 22.5% of the bill, and no log line looks broken. The API is fine. The integration is the bill.
Every generated second should be reserved before it is requested and accounted for after it is made.
Wan3.0 does not answer in the same HTTP request that asks for the video.
The Wan3.0 Video Generation API Reference is explicit: you create a task with the X-DashScope-Async: enable header, receive output.task_id , then query the task until output.task_status reaches a final state (Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, Wan3.0 Video Generation API Reference, accessed Nov 13, 2026). The reference suggests polling about every 15 seconds. Task IDs and the returned video_url are valid for 24 hours, after which the video is purged.
That contract has three consequences for a platform team:
So the unit of work is a job record with a lifecycle, not an API call. Article 06 in this series follows a video team's pipeline and review gates; this article is the code layer underneath, written for the engineer who owns it.
Wiring Wan3.0 into an internal tool this quarter? Walk through your task states, polling and archive path with the Wan team before the first producer gets an API key: Map your job states before launch →
Five components, each with one job, keep the integration boring.
Five components for a Wan3.0 integration; field names in code style come from the API reference. (Wan.)
Only the submitter can spend money. Product code never calls create directly; it inserts a job and walks away.
One code path spends; every other path reads.
The most expensive bug in a video generation API integration is invisible.
I call it the orphan task : a generation the provider created, and can bill, whose task_id your system never recorded. The create call succeeds on the server, the response never reaches your code, and a retry creates a second task for the same take.
The reference itself says it plainly: "Do not create duplicate tasks. Instead, use polling to retrieve the result." The reference documents no idempotency field on the create request, so the guarantee has to live on your side.
The UNCERTAIN state is the honest part. If you cannot know whether a task was created, do not guess by creating another.
Park, alert, decide. Park the job, alert its owner, and let a person decide. A stuck job costs one manual decision; a blind resubmit may cost a second billed generation.
When the create call's outcome is unknown, stop: never pay twice to find out.

items.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.
The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.
Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:
Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.
Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.
Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.
Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

items.title: “AI央行”大地震，冲击会沿融资链传多远？
items.detailText:
黄仁勋辞职引发对英伟达AI金融网络系统性风险的担忧
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋突然辞职，引发了一个令人担忧的问题：如果这家芯片巨头陷入困境，冲击会不会沿着它为支撑人工智能（AI）热潮而搭建的、环环相扣的金融网络蔓延？
为推动AI行业发展，英伟达已向其他企业作出数千亿美元的财务承诺，获得了“AI央行”的称号。因此，一旦英伟达出现严重问题，可能给美国经济和金融市场带来深远冲击。
早在7月，美国真正的央行——美联储官员就已讨论过， 如果AI行业出现问题，资产价格是否会出现“大范围重估”。
分析师以及现任和前任金融官员认为，2007至2008年金融危机重演的可能性不大。
曾执掌美国联邦存款保险公司（FDIC）的前监管官员希Sheila Bair认为，从银行监管的角度看，英伟达完全谈不上“大而不能倒”。
英伟达不会像陷入困境的银行那样容易受到信心骤失的冲击。即使出了问题，它仍能生产客户愿意购买的产品，庞大的股权价值也为其提供了缓冲。
不过，Bair指出，监管机构需要密切关注银行及整个金融体系对英伟达及类似企业的风险敞口，“如果英伟达倒下，那将是一场相当大的地震。”
投资者仍对英伟达寄予厚望，该公司将于下周二公布财报。LSEG的数据显示，分析师预计，英伟达本财年营收将增至上一财年的两倍以上，并在随后两年里再翻近一番。
但黄仁勋的离职，使公司前景变得格外难以预测。自1993年参与创立英伟达以来，黄仁勋一直领导这家公司。截至周四上午，英伟达股价较10月6日的峰值下跌超三成。
不过，密切追踪AI行业资金流向的人士认为，即使英伟达股价进一步大跌，也不太可能引发监管机构所防范的那类系统性问题。
他们关注的是，推动这轮繁荣的多项因素会不会同时逆转。例如，如果英伟达GPU芯片的价值下跌，投资者可能会开始怀疑，那些借钱购买芯片的企业能否偿还债务。
届时，大型科技公司向业内其他企业提供的资金支持，可能突然成为自身增长的拖累。科技公司将同时面临信用压力和股价下跌。科技巨头一旦陷入困境，冲击可能从科技股投资组合蔓延至整个经济。
“我认为这确实值得担忧，因为实体经济和金融市场都依赖同一个增长支柱。一旦市场下跌，两者可能相互拖累，放大冲击，”国际货币基金组织（IMF）负责全球市场分析部门的助理主任Jason Wu说。
Wu是IMF于10月发布的《全球金融稳定报告》中一个章节的主要作者。该章节警告，AI企业和投资者不断加杠杆，可能引发更广泛的问题。
在规模达15万亿美元的投资级债券市场上，“超大规模云服务商”（即体量最大的几家科技公司）占债券发行量的比重仅用两年就从1%升至10%。
对冲基金和散户投资者也在通过借钱买股票或投资内嵌杠杆的基金，进一步放大原本就有风险的押注。
英伟达处在这张金融网络的中心。它多次为规模较小的AI云服务商提供支持。这些被称为“新云”（neoclouds）的企业使用英伟达芯片建设数据中心，再将算力出租给其他公司。
英伟达7月披露，其承诺包括向这类企业采购最多360亿美元的云服务。这既能帮助英伟达为AI芯片拓展客户，也让这些云服务商更容易获得融资。
IMF的Wu等人将这类安排称为“循环融资”。业务增长时，大公司帮助客户购买自己的产品，可以推动业务发展。但如果英伟达无法履行承诺，冲击就会传导至借款企业及相关放贷银行。
透明度相对较低的私募信贷基金也为这轮AI热潮提供了大量贷款。一旦市场逆转，这些基金会受到多大冲击，仍是监管机构讨论的问题。
英伟达没有披露具体合作伙伴，但CoreWeave、IREN等新云服务商已各自披露了与英伟达的合作关系。
最近几周，不少新云服务商面临压力。LSEG数据显示，10月1日至11月5日，以信用违约互换（CDS）利差衡量的CoreWeave债务违约保护成本上升了94%，接近翻倍，随后趋于稳定。
11月3日至5日，IREN一只2029年到期的可转债价格下跌23%，同期公司股价下跌26%。
英伟达的其他承诺还包括，在满足特定条件的情况下，为OpenAI和SB Energy计划在俄亥俄州建设的一项大型数据中心项目分阶段提供总额1050亿美元的担保。
英伟达还承诺，为华尔街金融机构一项规模达5000亿美元的信贷计划提供最高1250亿美元的兜底支持。
这些承诺形式各异，部分可能无需实际履行，即便触发，也不太可能同时到期。哥伦比亚商学院金融学教授Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh估计，这些承诺合计约4000亿美元。
Nieuwerburgh说道：“这家公司得走到生死存亡的边缘，这些担保才会全部受到威胁。要说这个体系是安全的，我不愿这么下结论。但眼下，整个体系里确实有大量股权资本。”
过去几天，英伟达的股价走势与多数新云服务商出现分化。英伟达股价本周下跌，多数新云服务商的股价却已反弹。这表明，至少目前，投资者认为问题主要出在英伟达自身。
与此同时，芯片业务的丰厚利润正吸引其他企业进入英伟达所在的市场。Nieuwerburgh说，AMD、博通、英特尔、谷歌、微软和OpenAI都在推进自研AI芯片。
随着时间推移，这些芯片有可能替代英伟达的产品，从而限制英伟达（如果）陷入困境所造成的经济冲击。
但Nieuwerburgh补充说，仍无法完全排除AI投资热潮突然熄火所带来的金融风险。他说，各国央行官员“显然非常、非常、非常焦虑，也在认真思考这些问题”。
